title: Exam Week
subtitle: Ten weeks, one paper. This is the practice run, and it is meant to be long.
objectives: Recall the mixtures and separation work from weeks 1 to 4
Recall the forces work from weeks 5 and 6
Recall the energy work from weeks 7 to 9
Sit a full-length paper at exam pace

cards.title: Everything from this term, in one go
cards.text: Twenty-four questions. Longer than a normal week on purpose, because the real paper will be too.

cards.title: Mixtures: it all comes down to size
cards.text: Four weeks, one thread. How big the pieces are decides everything else.
points: **Under 1 nm** dissolves — a solution.
**1 to 1000 nm** floats — a colloid.
**Over 1000 nm** settles — a suspension.
**Separation method** follows from which one you have.

question.text: Which method would separate salt from water?
question.explain: Dissolved salt passes every filter. Only a change of state gets the water away from it.

cards.title: Forces: stillness means balance
cards.text: Nothing at rest is free of forces. It is holding a draw.
points: **Gravity** acts between masses. Mass stays; weight changes.
**Friction** resists sliding, and static beats kinetic.
**Normal force** is the surface pushing back.
**Buoyancy** depends on displaced weight, not the material.

cards.title: Ten weeks, one board
cards.text: Tap each week. The second line is the trap it sets.

cards.title: One fan, most of the term
cards.text: If you forget a definition, picture the fan and walk through it.
points: **Energy chain** — electrical, magnetic, kinetic, plus heat and sound.
**Friction** — bearings, and what happens when they dry out.
**Simple machines** — gears, screws and a wedge for a blade.
**Winnowing** — a wind you can switch on.

question.text: Why is starting a heavy box moving harder than keeping it moving?
options: Static friction is greater than kinetic friction
question.explain: Static has to be beaten first. Once sliding, the smaller kinetic friction applies.

cards.title: Good spot to pause
cards.text: Half the review done. The energy weeks are next, then the paper.

cards.title: Energy: it changes form and leaks
cards.text: Nothing is destroyed. Some always leaves as a form you did not want.
points: **Kinetic and potential** trade places in every fall and throw.
**Speed is squared**; mass is only proportional.
**A circuit** needs a source, conductors, a switch and a load.
**Every transformation** loses some to heat and sound.

cards.title: The one rule that keeps coming back
cards.text: If you remember nothing else from the term, remember what squaring does.
points: **Double the speed**, four times the kinetic energy.
**Double the mass**, only twice.
**Braking distance** follows the same curve.
**It decided** meteors, wind and cars alike.

cards.title: The whole term on one bench
cards.alt: A school science bench with a filter funnel, a magnet and sand, a beaker, a pulley, a ramp with a toy car, and a thermometer
cards.text: Filter, magnet, beaker, pulley, ramp, thermometer. Name the week each one belongs to.

cards.title: Machines: a trade, never a gift
cards.text: Less force always costs more distance. The energy does not improve.
points: **Six simple machines**, everything else a combination.
**Mechanical advantage** multiplies force, not energy.
**A screw** is a ramp wound round a post.
**Your arm** trades force away to buy speed.

question.text: A ramp lets you use half the force. What does it cost?
question.explain: Force down, distance up. The product is fixed.

cards.title: Before the paper, the boring advice that works
cards.text: None of this is about being clever on the day.
points: **Sleep beats cramming.** Memory is consolidated while you sleep.
**Eat something.** Your brain runs on glucose and nothing else.
**Read the whole question** before touching an option.
**Mark the hard one and move on.** Come back at the end.

cards.title: The four threads
points: Mixtures: particle size decides the class and the method.
Forces: at rest means balanced, not absent.
Energy: changes form, never destroyed, always leaks a little.
Machines: force traded against distance, every time.

quiz.text: A mixture whose particles are 1 to 1000 nm across is a…
quiz.explain: Too big to dissolve, too small to settle.
quiz.objective: Recall the mixtures and separation work from weeks 1 to 4

quiz.text: Why does a colloid not settle?
options: Molecular bombardment keeps the particles up
quiz.explain: Brownian motion. Gravity still pulls, but the knocking wins.
quiz.objective: Recall the mixtures and separation work from weeks 1 to 4

quiz.text: A visible torch beam through a liquid means…
options: the particles are colloid-sized or bigger
quiz.explain: The Tyndall effect. Solutions are far too fine to scatter light.
quiz.objective: Recall the mixtures and separation work from weeks 1 to 4

quiz.text: Muddy water left standing overnight separates by…
quiz.explain: Gravity pulls the suspended solids down into a layer.
quiz.objective: Recall the mixtures and separation work from weeks 1 to 4

quiz.text: What does a filter never remove?
quiz.explain: Dissolved substances are single molecules, smaller than any hole.
quiz.objective: Recall the mixtures and separation work from weeks 1 to 4

quiz.text: Winnowing separates by…
quiz.explain: Moving air carries the light pieces off and the heavy ones drop.
quiz.objective: Recall the mixtures and separation work from weeks 1 to 4

quiz.text: A magnet will attract…
quiz.explain: Iron, nickel and cobalt. Being a metal is not enough.
quiz.objective: Recall the mixtures and separation work from weeks 1 to 4

quiz.text: Distillation keeps which part?
quiz.explain: You collect the condensed liquid. Evaporation alone would keep the solid.
quiz.objective: Recall the mixtures and separation work from weeks 1 to 4

quiz.text: Rectification is…
options: distillation repeated many times for a purer result
quiz.explain: A tall column stacks many boil-and-condense cycles.
quiz.objective: Recall the mixtures and separation work from weeks 1 to 4

quiz.text: Your mass on the Moon is…
quiz.explain: Mass never changes with place. Only weight does.
quiz.objective: Recall the forces work from weeks 5 and 6

quiz.text: Astronauts float because…
options: they are in free fall around Earth
quiz.explain: Gravity up there is about ninety percent of surface gravity.
quiz.objective: Recall the forces work from weeks 5 and 6

quiz.text: Static friction is greater than kinetic friction.
quiz.explain: Which is why a box gives suddenly and then slides more easily.
quiz.objective: Recall the forces work from weeks 5 and 6

quiz.text: Why does a steel ship float?
options: The hull encloses air, so it displaces more weight than the ship has
quiz.explain: Shape decides it, not material. Crushed flat, the same steel sinks.
quiz.objective: Recall the forces work from weeks 5 and 6

quiz.text: A book rests on a table. Which forces balance?
quiz.explain: Gravity down, table up, nothing moves.
quiz.objective: Recall the forces work from weeks 5 and 6

quiz.text: A rope can apply…
quiz.explain: Rope pulls. It cannot push.
quiz.objective: Recall the forces work from weeks 5 and 6

quiz.text: Doubling an object's speed multiplies its kinetic energy by…
quiz.explain: Speed is squared. Mass is only proportional.
quiz.objective: Recall the energy work from weeks 7 to 9

quiz.text: At the top of a thrown ball's arc it has…
quiz.explain: Kinetic energy is momentarily zero; potential is at its highest.
quiz.objective: Recall the energy work from weeks 7 to 9

quiz.text: Heat from the Sun reaches Earth by…
quiz.explain: Space is nearly empty, so only radiation can cross it.
quiz.objective: Recall the energy work from weeks 7 to 9

quiz.text: An electric fan lowers the temperature of a closed room.
quiz.explain: The motor adds heat. It cools people by speeding evaporation, not the room.
quiz.objective: Recall the energy work from weeks 7 to 9

quiz.text: The energy chain in a fan motor is…
quiz.explain: The magnetic step is where the work actually happens.
quiz.objective: Recall the energy work from weeks 7 to 9

quiz.text: Which four roles are in every circuit?
quiz.explain: Something pushes, carries, decides and uses.
quiz.objective: Recall the energy work from weeks 7 to 9

quiz.text: A screw is really a…
options: inclined plane wrapped round a cylinder
quiz.explain: Follow the thread and you are walking a long gentle ramp.
quiz.objective: Recall simple machines from week 10

quiz.text: Mechanical advantage means a machine…
options: multiplies force at the cost of distance
quiz.explain: The trade. Energy in equals energy out, minus losses.
quiz.objective: Recall simple machines from week 10

quiz.text: A machine can give out more energy than it takes in.
quiz.explain: Never. Output is input minus friction losses.
quiz.objective: Recall simple machines from week 10

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 11 Science, the practice paper. Twenty-four questions spanning all ten teaching weeks, with the review cards organised by thread rather than by week number — mixtures as a size question, forces as a balance question, energy as a conversion question, machines as a trade. The fan card is a deliberate memory hook: almost every strand of the term appears somewhere in an appliance he has taken apart himself, so a forgotten definition has a physical object to hang on. The exam-technique card is in the review rather than the quiz because it is advice, not content.
discussion: Which four threads does the whole term come down to?
How much of this term can you find inside a fan?
Which topic would you want one more day on?
extension: Sit the quiz once at normal pace, then again a few days later without revising first.
Write your own exam question for each of the four threads.
misconceptions: That revision means re-reading. Testing yourself beats it.
That cramming the night before works better than sleeping.
